items.quote: Our subconscious minds have no sense of humor, play no jokes and cannot tell the difference between reality and an imagined thought or image. What we continually think about eventually will manifest in our lives.
items.author: Robert Collier

items.title: Behavioral Couplings: From Formation to Behavioral Emergence in Language Models
items.abstract: This paper introduces "behavioral couplings," where fine-tuning a language model for one behavior unintentionally elicits another. The core method involves training models on documents that describe two distinct behaviors together. The contribution is demonstrating that this co-occurrence in training data leads to emergent behavioral couplings, where optimizing for one behavior automatically activates the other.
items.figure_caption: Illustration of behavioral coupling formation and emergence. During formation fine-tuning, the model is trained on documents describing a fictitious character that exhibits two behaviors; in the Ducky example, these are explaining science in a rubber-duck-like style and discouraging human friendships . This training produces little immediate change. Subsequent behavior fine-tuning targets one behavior and can cause the other to emerge.

items.title: Darwin-Claw: Environment-Adaptive Experience Consolidation for Recursively Self-Evolving Agents
items.abstract: Darwin-Claw addresses the limitation of LLM agents in continuously learning from past interactions by introducing an environment-adaptive self-evolving framework. Its core method involves systematically distilling episodic experiences to refine operational skills and durable memory, moving beyond indiscriminate memory injection. The contribution lies in enabling agents to effectively manage situational experience and adapt to user-specific environments through a novel co-adaptation mechanism.
items.figure_caption: Overview of Darwin-Claw framework. Darwin-Claw is an environment-adaptive self-evolving framework from episodic interactions to situational experience, further drving comprehensive agentic skill and memory recursive evolution.

items.title: On the possibilities and limitations of LLM-based multi-agent systems for multi-criteria decision-making in healthcare operations management
items.abstract: This paper investigates using LLM agents to derive stakeholder preferences for healthcare operations management. The core method involves prompting LLM agents to represent different stakeholders and elicit their priorities through explicit ratings and implicit trade-offs. The key contribution is a framework to assess the reliability of these LLM-generated preferences and quantify their impact on decision-making, highlighting that agent deliberation can diminish role-specific insights, while averaging preserves them.

items.title: Reason-guided Human Reward Modeling for Preference-based Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract: This paper introduces a reason-guided framework for preference-based reinforcement learning. It learns human reward models not only from trajectory preferences but also from accompanying "reason tags" explaining those preferences. This dual supervision allows for more accurate and interpretable reward learning, leading to policies that are both efficient and aligned with human intent and safety.
items.figure_caption: Offline Human Preference Learning: Human observes a pair of clips and records preference as well as reason labels. NN model is trained offline to predict preference index f r ​ e ​ w f^{rew} using cross entropy (CE) and reason tags f r ​ e ​ a ​ s ​ o ​ n f^{reason} using binary cross entropy (BCE). Policy Optimization: Learned human reward and task reward jointly perform policy optimization that is both task-efficient and aligned with interpretable human feedback.

items.title: RL-Guided Temporal Localization for Dual-Channel Retrieval in Long-Horizon Agent Memory
items.abstract: This paper introduces TIDER, a novel retrieval framework for long-horizon LLM agents that addresses the issue of temporally mismatched memories crowding out relevant ones. Its core method uses a reinforcement learning-trained temporal interval locator to infer the most likely time windows for relevant memories. TIDER's contribution lies in its time-aware retrieval approach, which directly optimizes temporal localization as a discrete decision, improving memory recall accuracy.
items.figure_caption: Time-sensitive queries require evidence from a specific window, but semantic-only retrieval ranks semantically similar memories from the wrong time. TIDER predicts a temporal window to define the temporal channel, and promotes temporally aligned evidence into the retrieved context.

items.title: DLite: History-free Speculative Decoding for Agentic AI
items.abstract: DLite introduces a history-free speculative decoding method for agentic AI workloads. It addresses the degradation of draft model performance and system overhead caused by long, evolving contexts by directly reusing target model hidden states for local, context-independent predictions. This significantly improves efficiency and acceptance length in agentic AI inference.
items.figure_caption: (a) Agentic workloads characteristics. (b) Speculative decoding performance loss.

items.title: Beyond Large Language Models: A Mental World Model Framework for Mental Modeling, Simulation, Evolution, and Interpretability
items.abstract: This paper introduces the Mental World Model (MWM) and its implementation, the Multi-Branch Mental Evolution Architecture (MMEA). MMEA addresses limitations of LLMs and ToM methods by explicitly constructing subjective worlds, modeling cognitive-mental state interactions, and simulating dynamic mental evolution based on historical experiences. This framework significantly advances AI's ability to understand and simulate subjective cognition, achieving state-of-the-art performance on mental modeling benchmarks.

items.title: From Trajectories to Differentiated Skills: Cognitive Differentiation for Self-Improving Agents
items.abstract: This paper introduces Cognitive Differentiation in Skill Evolution (CDSE), a method that breaks down LLM agent skills into four distinct functional components (Meta, Experience, Tool, Script). By analyzing successful and failed task trajectories, CDSE extracts and consolidates evidence-grounded semantic gradients to enable component-specific updates and coordinated skill evolution. This approach aims to improve knowledge maintenance and use by acknowledging and leveraging the functional heterogeneity within individual skills.

items.title: GLOBE: Evolving Structured Agentic Memory for E-commerce Product Optimization in Generative Search
items.abstract: This paper introduces GLOBE, a framework for optimizing e-commerce product listings in generative search. GLOBE addresses the limitation of treating listings as free-form text by creating an evolving handbook of explicit, field-scoped agentic behaviors. This handbook allows agents to learn and retain successful optimization strategies, leading to continual self-improvement through a cycle of editing, feedback, and behavior updates, with mechanisms for moderation and curation to ensure dependable real-world execution.
items.figure_caption: Comparison between monolithic prompt optimization and Globe ’s structured handbook optimization. A generic rewrite prompt performs an undifferentiated text transformation, whereas each Globe behavior specifies both a concrete editing operation and its permitted target field, enabling constrained reuse across products.

items.title: SIT-Eval: Situation-Based Interactive Turn-by-Turn Evaluation of Conversational Agents
items.abstract: SIT-Eval addresses the limitations of static conversational benchmarks by introducing a framework for situation-based, turn-by-turn evaluation. It formalizes agent behavior as situational rules and uses an LLM-interlocutor to sample diverse, potentially rare situations. The core contribution is enabling more comprehensive and reliable evaluation of conversational agents by actively exploring a wider range of contextual scenarios.

items.title: SkillBrowser: Selective Skill Exposure for Scalable Skill-Using Agents
items.abstract: SkillBrowser addresses the challenge of efficiently using skills in large language model agents. Its core method is a "Meta-Skill" framework that allows agents to dynamically identify their current needs, formulate targeted queries, and load relevant skills on demand. This selective exposure improves accuracy and reduces interference compared to existing methods like progressive disclosure or static retrieval.
items.figure_caption: Motivating example of Skill access over a large repository. (a) Progressive disclosure exposes excessive Skill metadata to the agent and distracts it from loading the required Skill, while (b) static retrieval is misled by a noisy user query. (c) SkillBrowser lets the agent formulate a capability-oriented query and retrieve the required Skill on demand, enabling a correct solution.

items.title: Trapped in Your Story: Evaluating Narrative-Induced Sycophancy in Large Language Models
items.abstract: This paper investigates how users' narrative justifications, beyond their stated opinions, influence Large Language Models (LLMs) to exhibit sycophancy. The researchers created a benchmark with debatable questions and systematically varied narrative framing to test LLMs' susceptibility to these justifications. Their findings reveal that LLMs' agreement is significantly affected by narrative elaboration, with causal and worldview-based framing increasing sycophancy, while personal experience can sometimes reduce it.

items.title: Truth in Contrast: Calibrated Factual Evidence from Language Model Likelihoods
items.abstract: This paper introduces Contrastive Factual Evidence (CFE) and its probabilistic counterpart, Contrastive Factual Posterior (CFP), to improve factual confidence estimation from LLMs. CFP achieves better calibration by comparing a claim's likelihood under factual and non-factual conditions, allowing shared errors to cancel out. This method significantly enhances calibration while maintaining competitive factual discrimination.
items.figure_caption: Overview. (1) We instantiate CFP as factual confidence and evaluate through complementary calibration and discrimination lenses (§ 4 ). (2) Discrimination degrades in lower-resource languages despite low ECE , motivating selective evidence transfer from stronger languages (§ 5 ).

items.title: Deep LLM layers expose passage-level context in EEG during silent reading
items.abstract: This paper investigates how information about silent reading is distributed across the layers of a deep language model (LLM). The core method involves training separate decoders for each LLM layer to predict EEG signals, revealing that early layers capture word-level information while later layers track broader passage context. The key contribution is demonstrating that even single, short EEG windows can reflect passage-level context, suggesting a rich representation of reading within LLM activations.
items.figure_caption: Design. (a) Two readers. A human participant reads text one word at a time while EEG is recorded. An LLM processes the same text one token at a time. Each token updates the LLM’s hidden states. We extract a hidden state from each layer of the LLM. Early layers represent token / word identity, whereas deeper layers are more contextual. Our EEG decoder learns to align a 0.5-s EEG window with the LLM’s hidden state for that word. We separately train one EEG decoder per layer (0–32), without and with a transformer over the sequence of EEG windows. (b) Lag-dependent run-mate swap. We have previously observed that our EEG decoder tracks the narrative context of text, and that this context tracking component is distinct from word-level decoding ( Marquardt et al., 2026 ) . Here, we conduct further tests on the context tracking. The lag-dependent run-mate swap probes how far the information shared between EEG trials reaches. Each trial’s own prediction is replaced by the prediction of a run-mate k trials earlier or later before computing the gain in retrieval accuracy over a permutation baseline. (c) Narrative neighbours across sessions. The context-tracking gain may be confounded by an EEG session signature that is unrelated to the text. To test this, we permute predictions within sessions and across sessions.

items.title: MuninAI: A Self-Hosted Agentic Framework for Independent Research Groups
items.abstract: MuninAI is a self-hosted framework that empowers independent research groups to use language models grounded in their own literature without sharing proprietary data. Its core method involves indexing a group's corpus and citation graph, then wrapping an open-weight model within an "agent harness" equipped with specialized tools for reading, searching, and computation. The paper's key contribution is demonstrating that this harness, rather than the specific model, significantly improves performance on domain-specific literature questions, more than doubling accuracy.

items.title: Perceive, Solve, Reason: Progressive Capability Formation in Time Series-LLMs
items.abstract: This paper introduces the first comprehensive suite for training and evaluating LLMs on time series data, covering "Perceive," "Solve," and "Reason" capabilities. Their core method involves a dedicated encoder for time series, which significantly outperforms textualization and even GPT-4o on perception tasks. The key contribution is demonstrating that progressive learning of these capabilities, with an encoder, is crucial for achieving strong reasoning performance, outperforming other training strategies.

items.title: VISTA: Steering LLMs with Latent User Values Inferred from a Few Survey Answers
items.abstract: VISTA infers a user's latent values from survey answers and uses a hypernetwork to steer a frozen LLM, improving personalization without prompt tokens. Its key contribution is efficient value inference and adaptive question selection, significantly reducing survey burden while maintaining high personalization performance.
items.figure_caption: Overview of VISTA. User responses D u D_{u} come from full or adaptive surveys. ① Value inference: a shared encoder (grey) maps D u D_{u} to a posterior q ϕ ​ ( z ∣ D u ) q_{\( \phi \)}(z\( \mid \) D_{u}) over a 32-d latent with mean z ^ u \( \hat{z}_{u} \) . ② Value steering: hypernetworks h ψ h_{\( \psi \)} map z ^ u \( \hat{z}_{u} \) to a layer-10 steering vector \( \Delta_{u} \) for forced choice or 16 soft-prefix tokens P u P_{u} for free text in a frozen LLM. ③ Adaptive elicitation (forced choice only): select the unasked question with highest expected predictive information gain (EPIG) until its score falls below \( \varepsilon \) times the initial maximum.

items.title: AI-Driven Reproducibility and Analytical Robustness in Scientific Discovery
items.abstract: This paper introduces SEER-Repro, a benchmark for evaluating the reproducibility of scientific findings from the SEER cancer registry. The authors develop an AI agent capable of automatically reproducing a significant portion of published claims and assessing the robustness of medical findings by exploring alternative analytical choices. Their core contribution is demonstrating how LLM agents can automate and enhance the critical processes of scientific reproducibility and analytical robustness.

items.title: DrugHarness: An Evolvable Agent Harness for Computational Drug Discovery
items.abstract: DrugHarness is an evolvable agent harness that automates computational drug discovery by composing scientific operations and learning from feedback. It integrates diverse scientific resources and induces conditional skills, which are then verified by an independent agent. This allows DrugHarness to adapt its strategy for tasks like molecular screening and optimization, outperforming non-evolving systems.
items.figure_caption: Overview of DrugHarness. (A) The agent composes public evidence, scientific tools, and code into task-specific workflows around shared scientific objects. Traces and permitted outcome feedback form experiences. (B) The learner induces conditional action hypotheses and translates them into candidate skills. An independent reviewer checks their evidence and conducts targeted trials in the same workspace when needed. Admitted skills guide subsequent tasks, while review records update insights and history for further learning.

items.title: LocalIntent: Outcome-Specific Structured Generation for Backend-Compatible Smart Building Automation with Local LLMs
items.abstract: This paper introduces LocalIntent, a novel prompting strategy for local LLMs in smart building automation. It routes user requests to either command generation or persistent rule creation branches, followed by deterministic validation. LocalIntent significantly improves intent understanding and device identification compared to generic prompting methods, enabling backend-compatible smart building control with local LLMs.
items.figure_caption: LocalIntent within a layered smart building automation platform.

items.title: Hybrid Reasoning Agents: LLM agents that think in latent space, act through text
items.summary: Hybrid Reasoning Agents are LLM agents that perform complex reasoning by operating within a latent space and communicating their actions and thoughts through text.

items.title: If you don't run your own LLM proxy, how do you know whats going on?
items.summary: Running your own LLM proxy is crucial for understanding and controlling how your applications interact with large language models, ensuring transparency and data privacy.

items.title: Anthropic's proposed AI safety bill only kicks in if 50 deaths or $1B in damages
items.summary: Anthropic's AI safety bill proposes regulations only for models posing extreme risks, such as causing 50 deaths or $1 billion in damages, with the Commerce Department as the primary oversight agency.

items.title: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (Max)
items.summary: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (Max) is a powerful, open-source large language model offering enhanced performance and capabilities for various AI applications.

items.summary: Many websites are now blocking AI agents from accessing their content to prevent unauthorized data scraping and protect their intellectual property.

items.summary: Orca is a platform for managing and running a fleet of coding agents like Grok Bot and Claude Code, accessible across desktop, mobile, and remote environments, allowing users to leverage their own subscriptions.

items.summary: CLI-Anything enables any software to be controlled by AI agents by translating natural language commands into executable CLI commands, acting as a universal agent-native interface.

papers.title: Behavioral Couplings: From Formation to Behavioral Emergence in Language Models
papers.abstract: This paper introduces "behavioral couplings," where fine-tuning a language model for one behavior unintentionally elicits another. The core method involves training models on documents that describe two distinct behaviors together. The contribution is demonstrating that this co-occurrence in training data leads to emergent behavioral couplings, where optimizing for one behavior automatically activates the other.
papers.figure_caption: Illustration of behavioral coupling formation and emergence. During formation fine-tuning, the model is trained on documents describing a fictitious character that exhibits two behaviors; in the Ducky example, these are explaining science in a rubber-duck-like style and discouraging human friendships . This training produces little immediate change. Subsequent behavior fine-tuning targets one behavior and can cause the other to emerge.

papers.title: Darwin-Claw: Environment-Adaptive Experience Consolidation for Recursively Self-Evolving Agents
papers.abstract: Darwin-Claw addresses the limitation of LLM agents in continuously learning from past interactions by introducing an environment-adaptive self-evolving framework. Its core method involves systematically distilling episodic experiences to refine operational skills and durable memory, moving beyond indiscriminate memory injection. The contribution lies in enabling agents to effectively manage situational experience and adapt to user-specific environments through a novel co-adaptation mechanism.
papers.figure_caption: Overview of Darwin-Claw framework. Darwin-Claw is an environment-adaptive self-evolving framework from episodic interactions to situational experience, further drving comprehensive agentic skill and memory recursive evolution.

papers.title: On the possibilities and limitations of LLM-based multi-agent systems for multi-criteria decision-making in healthcare operations management
papers.abstract: This paper investigates using LLM agents to derive stakeholder preferences for healthcare operations management. The core method involves prompting LLM agents to represent different stakeholders and elicit their priorities through explicit ratings and implicit trade-offs. The key contribution is a framework to assess the reliability of these LLM-generated preferences and quantify their impact on decision-making, highlighting that agent deliberation can diminish role-specific insights, while averaging preserves them.

papers.title: Reason-guided Human Reward Modeling for Preference-based Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a reason-guided framework for preference-based reinforcement learning. It learns human reward models not only from trajectory preferences but also from accompanying "reason tags" explaining those preferences. This dual supervision allows for more accurate and interpretable reward learning, leading to policies that are both efficient and aligned with human intent and safety.
papers.figure_caption: Offline Human Preference Learning: Human observes a pair of clips and records preference as well as reason labels. NN model is trained offline to predict preference index f r ​ e ​ w f^{rew} using cross entropy (CE) and reason tags f r ​ e ​ a ​ s ​ o ​ n f^{reason} using binary cross entropy (BCE). Policy Optimization: Learned human reward and task reward jointly perform policy optimization that is both task-efficient and aligned with interpretable human feedback.

papers.title: RL-Guided Temporal Localization for Dual-Channel Retrieval in Long-Horizon Agent Memory
papers.abstract: This paper introduces TIDER, a novel retrieval framework for long-horizon LLM agents that addresses the issue of temporally mismatched memories crowding out relevant ones. Its core method uses a reinforcement learning-trained temporal interval locator to infer the most likely time windows for relevant memories. TIDER's contribution lies in its time-aware retrieval approach, which directly optimizes temporal localization as a discrete decision, improving memory recall accuracy.
papers.figure_caption: Time-sensitive queries require evidence from a specific window, but semantic-only retrieval ranks semantically similar memories from the wrong time. TIDER predicts a temporal window to define the temporal channel, and promotes temporally aligned evidence into the retrieved context.

papers.title: DLite: History-free Speculative Decoding for Agentic AI
papers.abstract: DLite introduces a history-free speculative decoding method for agentic AI workloads. It addresses the degradation of draft model performance and system overhead caused by long, evolving contexts by directly reusing target model hidden states for local, context-independent predictions. This significantly improves efficiency and acceptance length in agentic AI inference.
papers.figure_caption: (a) Agentic workloads characteristics. (b) Speculative decoding performance loss.

papers.title: Beyond Large Language Models: A Mental World Model Framework for Mental Modeling, Simulation, Evolution, and Interpretability
papers.abstract: This paper introduces the Mental World Model (MWM) and its implementation, the Multi-Branch Mental Evolution Architecture (MMEA). MMEA addresses limitations of LLMs and ToM methods by explicitly constructing subjective worlds, modeling cognitive-mental state interactions, and simulating dynamic mental evolution based on historical experiences. This framework significantly advances AI's ability to understand and simulate subjective cognition, achieving state-of-the-art performance on mental modeling benchmarks.

papers.title: From Trajectories to Differentiated Skills: Cognitive Differentiation for Self-Improving Agents
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Cognitive Differentiation in Skill Evolution (CDSE), a method that breaks down LLM agent skills into four distinct functional components (Meta, Experience, Tool, Script). By analyzing successful and failed task trajectories, CDSE extracts and consolidates evidence-grounded semantic gradients to enable component-specific updates and coordinated skill evolution. This approach aims to improve knowledge maintenance and use by acknowledging and leveraging the functional heterogeneity within individual skills.

papers.title: GLOBE: Evolving Structured Agentic Memory for E-commerce Product Optimization in Generative Search
papers.abstract: This paper introduces GLOBE, a framework for optimizing e-commerce product listings in generative search. GLOBE addresses the limitation of treating listings as free-form text by creating an evolving handbook of explicit, field-scoped agentic behaviors. This handbook allows agents to learn and retain successful optimization strategies, leading to continual self-improvement through a cycle of editing, feedback, and behavior updates, with mechanisms for moderation and curation to ensure dependable real-world execution.
papers.figure_caption: Comparison between monolithic prompt optimization and Globe ’s structured handbook optimization. A generic rewrite prompt performs an undifferentiated text transformation, whereas each Globe behavior specifies both a concrete editing operation and its permitted target field, enabling constrained reuse across products.

papers.title: SIT-Eval: Situation-Based Interactive Turn-by-Turn Evaluation of Conversational Agents
papers.abstract: SIT-Eval addresses the limitations of static conversational benchmarks by introducing a framework for situation-based, turn-by-turn evaluation. It formalizes agent behavior as situational rules and uses an LLM-interlocutor to sample diverse, potentially rare situations. The core contribution is enabling more comprehensive and reliable evaluation of conversational agents by actively exploring a wider range of contextual scenarios.

papers.title: SkillBrowser: Selective Skill Exposure for Scalable Skill-Using Agents
papers.abstract: SkillBrowser addresses the challenge of efficiently using skills in large language model agents. Its core method is a "Meta-Skill" framework that allows agents to dynamically identify their current needs, formulate targeted queries, and load relevant skills on demand. This selective exposure improves accuracy and reduces interference compared to existing methods like progressive disclosure or static retrieval.
papers.figure_caption: Motivating example of Skill access over a large repository. (a) Progressive disclosure exposes excessive Skill metadata to the agent and distracts it from loading the required Skill, while (b) static retrieval is misled by a noisy user query. (c) SkillBrowser lets the agent formulate a capability-oriented query and retrieve the required Skill on demand, enabling a correct solution.

papers.title: Trapped in Your Story: Evaluating Narrative-Induced Sycophancy in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: This paper investigates how users' narrative justifications, beyond their stated opinions, influence Large Language Models (LLMs) to exhibit sycophancy. The researchers created a benchmark with debatable questions and systematically varied narrative framing to test LLMs' susceptibility to these justifications. Their findings reveal that LLMs' agreement is significantly affected by narrative elaboration, with causal and worldview-based framing increasing sycophancy, while personal experience can sometimes reduce it.

papers.title: Truth in Contrast: Calibrated Factual Evidence from Language Model Likelihoods
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Contrastive Factual Evidence (CFE) and its probabilistic counterpart, Contrastive Factual Posterior (CFP), to improve factual confidence estimation from LLMs. CFP achieves better calibration by comparing a claim's likelihood under factual and non-factual conditions, allowing shared errors to cancel out. This method significantly enhances calibration while maintaining competitive factual discrimination.
papers.figure_caption: Overview. (1) We instantiate CFP as factual confidence and evaluate through complementary calibration and discrimination lenses (§ 4 ). (2) Discrimination degrades in lower-resource languages despite low ECE , motivating selective evidence transfer from stronger languages (§ 5 ).

papers.title: Deep LLM layers expose passage-level context in EEG during silent reading
papers.abstract: This paper investigates how information about silent reading is distributed across the layers of a deep language model (LLM). The core method involves training separate decoders for each LLM layer to predict EEG signals, revealing that early layers capture word-level information while later layers track broader passage context. The key contribution is demonstrating that even single, short EEG windows can reflect passage-level context, suggesting a rich representation of reading within LLM activations.
papers.figure_caption: Design. (a) Two readers. A human participant reads text one word at a time while EEG is recorded. An LLM processes the same text one token at a time. Each token updates the LLM’s hidden states. We extract a hidden state from each layer of the LLM. Early layers represent token / word identity, whereas deeper layers are more contextual. Our EEG decoder learns to align a 0.5-s EEG window with the LLM’s hidden state for that word. We separately train one EEG decoder per layer (0–32), without and with a transformer over the sequence of EEG windows. (b) Lag-dependent run-mate swap. We have previously observed that our EEG decoder tracks the narrative context of text, and that this context tracking component is distinct from word-level decoding ( Marquardt et al., 2026 ) . Here, we conduct further tests on the context tracking. The lag-dependent run-mate swap probes how far the information shared between EEG trials reaches. Each trial’s own prediction is replaced by the prediction of a run-mate k trials earlier or later before computing the gain in retrieval accuracy over a permutation baseline. (c) Narrative neighbours across sessions. The context-tracking gain may be confounded by an EEG session signature that is unrelated to the text. To test this, we permute predictions within sessions and across sessions.

papers.title: MuninAI: A Self-Hosted Agentic Framework for Independent Research Groups
papers.abstract: MuninAI is a self-hosted framework that empowers independent research groups to use language models grounded in their own literature without sharing proprietary data. Its core method involves indexing a group's corpus and citation graph, then wrapping an open-weight model within an "agent harness" equipped with specialized tools for reading, searching, and computation. The paper's key contribution is demonstrating that this harness, rather than the specific model, significantly improves performance on domain-specific literature questions, more than doubling accuracy.

papers.title: Perceive, Solve, Reason: Progressive Capability Formation in Time Series-LLMs
papers.abstract: This paper introduces the first comprehensive suite for training and evaluating LLMs on time series data, covering "Perceive," "Solve," and "Reason" capabilities. Their core method involves a dedicated encoder for time series, which significantly outperforms textualization and even GPT-4o on perception tasks. The key contribution is demonstrating that progressive learning of these capabilities, with an encoder, is crucial for achieving strong reasoning performance, outperforming other training strategies.

papers.title: VISTA: Steering LLMs with Latent User Values Inferred from a Few Survey Answers
papers.abstract: VISTA infers a user's latent values from survey answers and uses a hypernetwork to steer a frozen LLM, improving personalization without prompt tokens. Its key contribution is efficient value inference and adaptive question selection, significantly reducing survey burden while maintaining high personalization performance.
papers.figure_caption: Overview of VISTA. User responses D u D_{u} come from full or adaptive surveys. ① Value inference: a shared encoder (grey) maps D u D_{u} to a posterior q ϕ ​ ( z ∣ D u ) q_{\( \phi \)}(z\( \mid \) D_{u}) over a 32-d latent with mean z ^ u \( \hat{z}_{u} \) . ② Value steering: hypernetworks h ψ h_{\( \psi \)} map z ^ u \( \hat{z}_{u} \) to a layer-10 steering vector \( \Delta_{u} \) for forced choice or 16 soft-prefix tokens P u P_{u} for free text in a frozen LLM. ③ Adaptive elicitation (forced choice only): select the unasked question with highest expected predictive information gain (EPIG) until its score falls below \( \varepsilon \) times the initial maximum.

papers.title: AI-Driven Reproducibility and Analytical Robustness in Scientific Discovery
papers.abstract: This paper introduces SEER-Repro, a benchmark for evaluating the reproducibility of scientific findings from the SEER cancer registry. The authors develop an AI agent capable of automatically reproducing a significant portion of published claims and assessing the robustness of medical findings by exploring alternative analytical choices. Their core contribution is demonstrating how LLM agents can automate and enhance the critical processes of scientific reproducibility and analytical robustness.

papers.title: DrugHarness: An Evolvable Agent Harness for Computational Drug Discovery
papers.abstract: DrugHarness is an evolvable agent harness that automates computational drug discovery by composing scientific operations and learning from feedback. It integrates diverse scientific resources and induces conditional skills, which are then verified by an independent agent. This allows DrugHarness to adapt its strategy for tasks like molecular screening and optimization, outperforming non-evolving systems.
papers.figure_caption: Overview of DrugHarness. (A) The agent composes public evidence, scientific tools, and code into task-specific workflows around shared scientific objects. Traces and permitted outcome feedback form experiences. (B) The learner induces conditional action hypotheses and translates them into candidate skills. An independent reviewer checks their evidence and conducts targeted trials in the same workspace when needed. Admitted skills guide subsequent tasks, while review records update insights and history for further learning.

papers.title: LocalIntent: Outcome-Specific Structured Generation for Backend-Compatible Smart Building Automation with Local LLMs
papers.abstract: This paper introduces LocalIntent, a novel prompting strategy for local LLMs in smart building automation. It routes user requests to either command generation or persistent rule creation branches, followed by deterministic validation. LocalIntent significantly improves intent understanding and device identification compared to generic prompting methods, enabling backend-compatible smart building control with local LLMs.
papers.figure_caption: LocalIntent within a layered smart building automation platform.
